contact_edits.before: The original play starts with the police threatening to break the heads of protesters and ends with a description of what sounds like kettling. Its main concerns are an intractable economic crisis and the thwarting of reform by special interests. It all seems, when you read it, blazingly topical. It has some of the same effect onstage but not as much, because the action, what there is of it, doesn't so much carry the ideas as buckle under them. That's true of both versions, though on consideration I prefer the original, ugly warts and all. The rewrite gives the final moment to Chavenders secretary. It doesn't mean much because, even though she's played by Mary Haney, we don't know anything about her. ? On the Rocks runs until Oct. 8. For tickets, call 1-800-511-7429 or visit shawfest.com.
